records.region: St. Elias Mountains, Yukon–Alaska; Hubbard Glacier and Russell Fiord setting.
records.material_pending_reason: The chosen Canadian opening and intermediate glacial traverse to the mapped U.S. Hubbard corridor lack readable original cartographic correspondence. The U.S. mainstem, eastern tributary and actual Russell Fiord ending are supported at terrain/corridor scale.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Hubbard Glacier identifies the mapped southern ice corridor. Russell Fiord identifies the actual rendered ending's receiving water. Neither is assigned as the name of the whole selected river-group object, and the Canadian headward selection lacks sufficient visual correspondence.
records.completion_scope: The complete U.S. portion, all of the eastern tributary and the actual Russell Fiord ending have bounded terrain/corridor correspondence. The chosen Canadian opening and intermediate traverse to the U.S. mapping boundary remain materially unestablished. This is one source-material-pending result, not a completed name-scope hold. An exact contemporary ice front, measured hydraulic route, or one uniform name on all glacial components was not required.
records.supported_name_scope: Hubbard Glacier identifies the mapped southern ice corridor. Russell Fiord identifies the actual rendered ending's receiving water. Neither is assigned as the name of the whole selected river-group object, and the Canadian headward selection lacks sufficient visual correspondence.

scope_limits: The source-labelled glacier and fiord are component identities, not evidence that the modeled selection is a single natural river.
No current flow direction, subglacial hydraulic link, exact ice-front boundary, shoreline date or formal registered name extent is established.
The last stored tributary endpoint is not the actual system terminal; the mainstem ending in Russell Fiord was used.
The 2005 visitor prose and 2025 firn-study prose provide regional context only. Unseen maps, search extracts and the unacquired study figure do not support selected-route geography.

records.candidate_name_role: Regional named receiving-river clue; not an established identity for the whole selected path
records.material_pending_reason: The selected Pracuúba lake passage and north exit, long northbound wetland connector, eastern lake/wetland transfer and actual coastal terminal are not continuously established. The mapped Flechal continuation farther north does not close these selected-route gaps.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The sources identify the Flechal/Flexal river in the Pracuúba–Amapá coastal setting. They do not establish that the selected lake passage, northbound wetland connector and eastward coastal ending form its continuous named course. Rio Amapá Pequeno is a separately named tributary in the sources and is not assigned to this selection.
records.completion_scope: All 54 parts of both mainstem fragments were considered. The western drainage corridor is supported; the Pracuúba lake through-passage, northern wetland connector, eastern turn and actual coast crossing remain incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: The sources identify the Flechal/Flexal river in the Pracuúba–Amapá coastal setting. They do not establish that the selected lake passage, northbound wetland connector and eastward coastal ending form its continuous named course. Rio Amapá Pequeno is a separately named tributary in the sources and is not assigned to this selection.

scope_limits: Continuous source correspondence remains unestablished through the chosen lake approach, Pracuúba lake passage and north exit.
The selected long northbound lowland connector cannot simply inherit the nearby Flechal label.

The selected eastward wetland crossing and actual coastal terminal differ from the clearly depicted northward Flechal continuation; this is a required correspondence gap, not a demand for exact bank alignment.
Rio Amapá Pequeno, Rio Macari and Igarapé do Garrote are distinct source-labelled components or neighbouring rivers, not alternate names automatically transferable to this selection.
The source spellings Flechal and Flexal are retained as observed variants in the study; no formal registry decision is asserted.

records.region: Northern Yukon, Canada; upper inland selection and Babbage River coastal corridor.
records.material_pending_reason: Independent original coverage is missing for the chosen western opening, long upper and middle course, and the complete joining sequence into the observed lower Babbage corridor.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The mapped lower Babbage River and Phillips Bay terminal only. The name is not assigned to the unexamined chosen western opening and upper-to-middle course, and a representative identity for the entire selection is not yet established.
records.completion_scope: Bounded source research is concluded with one source-material-pending primary state. Lower-route and coastal correspondence are preserved; the remaining upper and cross-sheet gaps prevent completed representative-system or naming-scope-hold classification. Accepted names remain null and application flags false.
records.supported_name_scope: The mapped lower Babbage River and Phillips Bay terminal only. The name is not assigned to the unexamined chosen western opening and upper-to-middle course, and a representative identity for the entire selection is not yet established.

naming_scope_details.unnamed_components: No name has been established for the unexamined chosen opening or upper/middle components.
naming_scope_details.no_unnamed_claim: Lack of an established component name in this pass does not imply absence of an Indigenous, local or official name.

records.region: Northern Río Negro interior, Argentina; southeast-trending selected internal-drainage corridor
records.material_pending_reason: The successfully inspected independent management-plan cartography covers an adjacent area to the south, rather than this selected corridor. It cannot establish the chosen opening, upper and middle through-links, possible depression passages or actual internal endpoint. The independently identified Reichler article original returned HTTP403 and no article content was read. Whole-route geographic correspondence therefore remains materially incomplete.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Río Negro in the assignment identifies the Argentine province. No evidence supports naming this selected interior line Río Negro. Nor is the neighboring Valcheta/Curicó identity from a previously researched target transferred to this selection.
records.completion_scope: A bounded source investigation and explicit component accounting were completed, but substantive geographic correspondence remains incomplete. All 37 stored parts are represented below. The missing evidence is ordinary corridor-scale continuity and terminal identity, not precise banks, modeled vertices, present flow or current water levels.
records.supported_name_scope: No river name is supported for a selected reach or for the whole selected system by material actually inspected in this bounded investigation.

scope_limits: The identity of the chosen headward opening and whether each selected upper and middle interval is an ordinary connected drainage.
Which channels, joins, lowland depressions or temporary-water passages are followed by the middle changes of direction.
The lower selected channel identity and the geographic identity of its actual internal endpoint.
Whether any local reach name or representative whole-system name can be supported after independent corridor evidence becomes available.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
